subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: plugin-emitted detectors and evals

question: Should external plugins be allowed to emit canonical `ai_safety.*` events, and what host-controlled authorization and provenance must distinguish those claims from core-trusted telemetry?
rationale: This creates a permanent public plugin contract whose output may drive security audits and operator decisions; source inspection cannot determine whether manifest declaration alone matches maintainers' intended trust model.

options.title: Approve a gated canonical API
options.body: Finalize https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107158 first, then permit external emission only with host-attested provenance, explicit capability authorization, schema validation, and clear untrusted-emitter metadata.

options.title: Keep canonical events core-only
options.body: Require external plugins to emit plugin-namespaced diagnostics or generic agent events, with only vetted core adapters translating them into canonical safety events.

options.title: Defer the taxonomy surface
options.body: Keep existing generic event APIs and pause the linked implementation until concrete operator and exporter requirements justify a stable canonical contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated canonical API
recommendation.body: Finalize https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/107158 first, then permit external emission only with host-attested provenance, explicit capability authorization, schema validation, and clear untrusted-emitter metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent relevant history hardened diagnostic trust metadata and internal plugin subscription boundaries.
